questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)?
o: The Home Minister of the State
questions.e: The Chief Minister of the state is the ex-officio chairperson of the SDMA.

questions.q: The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) is co-chaired by the Collector and:
o: The elected representative of the local authority
questions.e: The elected representative of the local authority is the ex-officio co-chairperson of the DDMA.

questions.q: The Bar Council of India (BCI) was established under which Act?
questions.e: The BCI was established under a legislation enacted by the Parliament, namely, the Advocates Act, 1961.

questions.q: Who are the ex-officio members of the Bar Council of India?
o: Attorney-General of India and Solicitor-General of India
Chief Justice of India and Law Minister
questions.e: The Attorney-General of India and the Solicitor-General of India are the ex-officio members of the BCI.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Chairman and Vice-Chairman of the Bar Council of India?
questions.e: The BCI shall have a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman elected by the Council for a period of two years.

questions.q: For a State Bar Council (SBC) with an electorate exceeding ten thousand, how many members are elected?
questions.e: In the case of a State Bar Council with an electorate of more than ten thousand, there are 25 members.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio member of a State Bar Council?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: In the case of any State Bar Council, the Advocate-General of the state is the ex-officio member.

questions.q: How long is the term of office for an elected member of a State Bar Council?
questions.e: The term of office of an elected member of any State Bar Council is five years.

questions.q: Which category of advocates is entitled to practice law before the Supreme Court only when instructed by an Advocate-on-Record?
questions.e: A Senior Advocate is not entitled to appear in the Supreme Court without an Advocate-on-Record.

questions.q: The 'Advocate-on-Record' system in the Supreme Court replaced which earlier system in 1954?
questions.e: In 1954, "Advocates-on-Record" replaced the system of "Agents" in the Supreme Court.

questions.q: To be eligible for the Advocate-on-Record examination, an advocate must have at least how many years of standing?
questions.e: Regulations state that an advocate must have received training from an Advocate-on-Record for at least ten years standing.

questions.q: According to Article 39A, the State shall provide free legal aid to ensure that justice is not denied by reason of:
questions.e: Article 39A directs the State to provide free legal aid to ensure justice is not denied by reason of economic or other disabilities.

questions.q: Which constitutional articles make it obligatory for the State to ensure equality before law and equal opportunity for justice?
questions.e: Articles 14 and 22(1) make it obligatory for the State to ensure equality before law and a legal system based on equal opportunity.

questions.q: NALSA frames economical schemes for which body to implement throughout the country?
questions.e: NALSA frames effective and economical schemes for the State Legal Services Authorities to implement Legal Services Programmes.

questions.q: Which of the following is included in 'free legal services' under the Legal Services Authorities Act? 1️⃣ Payment of court fee 2️⃣ Providing service of lawyers 3️⃣ Preparation of appeal papers 4️⃣ Translation of documents
questions.e: Free legal services include payment of court fees, providing lawyers, obtaining certified copies, and preparation/printing/translation of documents.

questions.q: Which of the following persons are eligible for free legal services? 1️⃣ Victims of trafficking 2️⃣ Disabled persons 3️⃣ Persons in custody 4️⃣ Members of SC/ST
questions.e: Eligible persons include victims of trafficking, disabled persons, persons in custody, and members of SC/ST.

questions.q: The Lok Adalat system is based on the principles of which Indian leader?
questions.e: The Lok Adalat system is based on Gandhian principles.

questions.q: Lok Adalats are considered a component of which system?
questions.e: Lok Adalat is one of the components of the ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution) system.

questions.q: Who can organize Lok Adalats at such intervals and places as it thinks fit? 1️⃣ State Legal Services Authority 2️⃣ High Court Legal Services Committee 3️⃣ Taluk Legal Services Committee
questions.e: The State, District, or Taluk Authorities, as well as Supreme Court or High Court Committees, may organize Lok Adalats.

questions.q: For the purpose of the Code of Criminal Procedure (1973), every Lok Adalat shall be deemed to be a:
questions.e: Every Lok Adalat shall be deemed to be a Civil Court for the purpose of the Code of Criminal Procedure (1973).

questions.q: Which type of Lok Adalat sits continuously for a set number of days to facilitate settlements?
questions.e: A Continuous Lok Adalat bench sits continuously for a set number of days to facilitate settlements.

questions.q: Which type of Lok Adalat is organized in a single day across ALL courts of a State?
questions.e: A Mega Lok Adalat is organized in the State on a single day in all courts of the State.

questions.q: One of the benefits of Lok Adalat is that if court fees have already been paid:
o: The amount will be refunded if the dispute is settled
They are transferred to the High Court
questions.e: There is no court fee, and if fee is already paid, the amount will be refunded if the dispute is settled at Lok Adalat.

questions.q: Permanent Lok Adalats were introduced by an amendment to the Legal Services Authorities Act in which year?
questions.e: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 was amended in 2002 to provide for Permanent Lok Adalats.

questions.q: A Permanent Lok Adalat Chairman must be or have been:
o: A District Judge or higher rank
questions.e: The Chairman must be or have been a district judge, additional district judge, or held higher judicial office.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a public utility service under the jurisdiction of Permanent Lok Adalats?
questions.e: Public utility services include transport, postal/phone, power/water, sanitation, hospitals, and insurance.

questions.q: If an application is made to a Permanent Lok Adalat, no party shall invoke the jurisdiction of:
o: Any court in the same dispute
questions.e: After an application is made, no party shall invoke the jurisdiction of any court in the same dispute.

questions.q: Permanent Lok Adalat awards are made by:
o: Majority of the persons constituting the body
questions.e: Every award shall be by a majority of the persons constituting the Permanent Lok Adalat.

questions.q: Which report (1974) of the Law Commission stressed a different approach for family disputes?
questions.e: The Law Commission in its 59th report (1974) stressed a radically different approach for family disputes.

questions.q: The Code of Civil Procedure was amended in 1976 to provide special procedures for which matters?
questions.e: The Code of Civil Procedure was amended in 1976 to provide for a special procedure in suits relating to family matters.

questions.q: Family Courts aim to provide which type of remedy?
questions.e: Objectives include providing an inexpensive remedy and having flexibility and an informal atmosphere.

questions.q: Family Courts have exclusive jurisdiction over: 1️⃣ Matrimonial relief 2️⃣ Guardianship of a person 3️⃣ Maintenance of wife 4️⃣ Property of spouses
questions.e: Jurisdiction includes matrimonial relief, property of spouses, legitimacy, guardianship/custody, and maintenance.

questions.q: During the reconciliation stage in a Family Court, which rules do NOT apply?
questions.e: During the reconciliation stage, proceedings will be informal and rigid rules of procedure shall not apply.

questions.q: The Gram Nyayalayas Act was enacted in which year?
questions.e: The Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008 was enacted to provide access to justice at the grass roots level.

questions.q: Who is the appointing authority for a Nyayadhikari?
o: The Chief Justice of High Court
questions.e: The presiding officer (Nyayadhikari) shall be appointed by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.

questions.q: A Gram Nyayalaya exercises the powers of which courts?
questions.e: The Gram Nyayalaya shall exercise the powers of both Criminal and Civil Courts.

questions.q: A person accused of an offence before a Gram Nyayalaya can file an application for:
questions.e: A person accused of an offence can file an application for plea bargaining.

questions.q: Is it mandatory for all States to set up Gram Nyayalayas under the 2008 Act?
o: Only for states with large tribal populations
Only if ordered by the High Court
questions.e: The Act does not make the setting-up of Gram Nyayalayas mandatory.

questions.q: Which Act provides for Commercial Divisions and Commercial Appellate Divisions in High Courts?
questions.e: The Commercial Courts Act, 2015 was enacted for the constitution of Commercial Courts and Divisions.

questions.q: Under the Commercial Courts Act, what is mandatory before institution of a suit that doesn't need urgent relief?
questions.e: A provision is made for compulsory mediation before institution of a suit which does not contemplate urgent interim relief.

questions.q: The item of 'Local Government' is mentioned in which list of the Seventh Schedule?
questions.e: The fifth entry of the State List of the Seventh Schedule deals with 'local government'.

questions.q: Which committee recommended a 'three-tier' panchayati raj system?
questions.e: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee recommended a three-tier system: gram panchayat, panchayat samiti, and zila parishad.

questions.q: In the Balwantrai Mehta model, who should be the chairman of the Zila Parishad?
questions.e: The committee recommended that the district collector should be the chairman of the zila parishad.

questions.q: Which state followed Rajasthan in adopting the Panchayati Raj system in 1959?
questions.e: Rajasthan was followed by Andhra Pradesh, which also adopted the system in 1959.

questions.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) was appointed by which government?
questions.e: In December 1977, the Janata Government appointed the Ashok Mehta Committee.

questions.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended that a ______ should be the first point for decentralization below state level.
questions.e: The committee recommended that a district should be the first point for decentralisation under popular supervision below the state level.

questions.q: Which committee recommended the creation of a 'District Development Commissioner' post?
questions.e: The G.V.K. Rao Committee recommended creating the post of District Development Commissioner to act as CEO of Zila Parishad.

questions.q: The L.M. Singhvi Committee called which body the "embodiment of direct democracy"?
questions.e: The L.M. Singhvi Committee emphasised the importance of the Gram Sabha and called it the embodiment of direct democracy.

questions.q: Which committee recommended that the District Collector should be the CEO of the Zila Parishad?
questions.e: The Thungon Committee recommended that the district collector should be the chief executive officer of the Zilla Parishad.

questions.q: The 73rd Amendment Act added which new schedule to the Constitution?
questions.e: The act added a new Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution, containing 29 functional items.

questions.q: Which Article defines 'Gram Sabha' under Part IX of the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 243A of the Constitution deals with the subject-matter of the Gram Sabha.

questions.q: According to the 73rd Amendment, the chairperson of a panchayat at which level shall be elected in such manner as the state legislature determines?
questions.e: The chairperson of a panchayat at the village level shall be elected in such manner as the state legislature determines.

questions.q: The Superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for panchayat elections are vested in:
questions.e: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the panchayats shall be vested in the state election commission.

questions.q: A State Finance Commission makes recommendations to the Governor regarding: 1️⃣ Distribution of net proceeds of taxes between state and panchayats 2️⃣ Determination of taxes assigned to panchayats 3️⃣ Grants-in-aid from the consolidated fund of the state
questions.e: The Finance Commission makes recommendations on the distribution of net proceeds of taxes, determination of taxes assigned to panchayats, and grants-in-aid.

questions.q: Which functional item is NOT listed under the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats?
questions.e: Fire services is an item under the Twelfth Schedule for municipalities. Agriculture , small-scale industries , and the public distribution system  are under the Eleventh Schedule.

questions.q: The PESA Act (1996) provides that every village shall have a Gram Sabha consisting of:
o: Persons whose names are in the electoral rolls for the village level Panchayat
questions.e: Every village shall have a Gram Sabha consisting of persons whose names are included in the electoral rolls for the Panchayat at the village level.

questions.q: Under PESA, the recommendations of which body are mandatory for the grant of prospecting licenses or mining leases for minor minerals in Scheduled Areas?
o: Gram Sabha or Panchayats at the appropriate level
questions.e: The recommendations of the Gram Sabha or the Panchayats at the appropriate level shall be mandatory for grant of prospecting licence or mining lease for minor minerals in the Scheduled Areas.

questions.q: In terms of Urban Local Government evolution, which resolution is called the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government?
questions.e: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 has been hailed as the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government.

questions.q: The 74th Amendment Act added which Schedule to the Constitution?
questions.e: The 74th Amendment Act has added a new Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution.

questions.q: Who specifies the density of population and revenue generated to categorize an area as a transitional, smaller, or larger urban area?
questions.e: The governor has to specify a transitional area, a smaller urban area or a larger urban area keeping in view factors like population and density.

questions.q: Which official is appointed by the state government and acts as the chief executive authority of a Municipal Corporation?
questions.e: The municipal commissioner is responsible for the implementation of decisions and is the chief executive authority of the corporation.

questions.q: The Central Council of Local Government consists of the Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and:
o: Ministers for local self-government in states
questions.e: The Council consists of the Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs in the Government of India and the ministers for local self-government in states.

questions.q: At present, how many Union Territories are there in India?
questions.e: At present, there are twenty-eight states and eight union territories.

questions.q: Which Union Territory was created in 2019 along with Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.e: In 2019, the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir was bifurcated into two separate union territories: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

questions.q: Who administers every Union Territory?
o: The Governor of the nearest state
The President acting through an administrator
questions.e: Every union territory is administered by the President acting through an administrator appointed by him/her.

questions.q: The President can make regulations for peace, progress and good government for which UTs? 1️⃣ Andaman and Nicobar Islands 2️⃣ Lakshadweep 3️⃣ Ladakh 4️⃣ Delhi
questions.e: The President can make regulations for Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu and Ladakh.

questions.q: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act provided special status to which Union Territory?
questions.e: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1991 provided a special status to the Union Territory of Delhi.

questions.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram?
questions.e: The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes in any state except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.q: Who is empowered to increase or decrease the area of a Scheduled Area?
questions.e: The President is empowered to declare an area to be a scheduled area and can also increase or decrease its area.

questions.q: The Election Commission of India is NOT concerned with elections to:
questions.e: The election commission is not concerned with the elections to panchayats and municipalities in the states.

questions.q: The UPSC consists of a chairman and other members appointed by:
questions.e: The UPSC consists of a chairman and other members appointed by the President of India.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Chairman and members of the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.e: The chairman and members of the Commission hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: The salaries, allowances, and pensions of UPSC members are charged on:
questions.e: The entire expenses including salaries, allowances and pensions of the chairman and members of the UPSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the functions of Public Service Commissions?
questions.e: Article 320 of the Constitution deals with the functions of Public Service Commissions.

questions.q: In the case of SPSC, the age limit for retirement is:
questions.e: The chairman and members of the SPSC hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 62 years.

questions.q: Although appointed by the Governor, the chairman and members of a SPSC can be removed ONLY by:
questions.e: Although the chairman and members of a SPSC are appointed by the governor, they can be removed only by the President.

questions.q: A Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) can be created by:
o: An Act of Parliament on request of state legislatures
questions.e: A JSPSC can be created by an act of Parliament on the request of the state legislatures concerned.

questions.q: Under which Article is the Finance Commission of India provided for?
questions.e: Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides for a Finance Commission.

questions.q: Who determines the qualifications and selection manner for Finance Commission members?
questions.e: The Constitution authorises the Parliament to determine the qualifications of members of the commission and the manner in which they should be selected.

questions.q: Which federal body was vested with powers to take all major decisions relating to GST?
questions.e: The GST Council is the first constitutional federal body vested with powers to take all major decisions relating to GST.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is established by which Article?
questions.e: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body directly established by Article 338 of the Constitution.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes was conferred constitutional status by which Amendment Act?
questions.e: The 102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred a constitutional status on the NCBC.

questions.q: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by:
questions.e: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is to be appointed by the President of India.

questions.q: Who is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.e: The CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

questions.q: The CAG holds office for a term of six years or until attaining the age of:
questions.e: The CAG holds office for a term of six years or upto the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: In practice, the CAG of India fulfills which role?
questions.e: In practice, the CAG is fulfilling the role of an Auditor-General only and not that of a Comptroller.

questions.q: Who is the highest law officer in India?
questions.e: The Attorney General for India is the highest law officer in the country.

questions.q: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of:
questions.e: The AG holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Who is the highest law officer in a State?
questions.e: The advocate general is the highest law officer in the state.

questions.q: Which institution was established as a 'Think Tank' to replace the Planning Commission?
questions.e: The NITI Aayog was established in 2015 as the successor to the planning commission and acts as the premier policy 'Think Tank'.

questions.q: Is NITI Aayog a constitutional body?
o: No, it is a non-constitutional body
questions.e: NITI Aayog is neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body; it is a non-constitutional or extra-constitutional body.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.e: The Chairperson of the NITI Aayog is the Prime Minister of India.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in which year?
questions.e: The NHRC was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.q: What is the retirement age for the Chairperson and members of the NHRC?
questions.e: The chairperson and members hold office for a term of three years or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: Are the recommendations of the NHRC binding on the government?
o: Only if approved by the President
Only in cases of custodial death
questions.e: The functions of the commission are mainly recommendatory in nature and its recommendations are not binding.

questions.q: Which body was constituted in 1992 for protecting and safeguarding the interests of women?
questions.e: The National Commission for Women was constituted in 1992 for protecting and safeguarding the interests and rights of women.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission (CIC) consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and not more than how many Information Commissioners?
questions.e: The Commission consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was conferred statutory status in which year?
questions.e: The CVC was conferred statutory status by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

questions.q: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) was constituted in which year?
questions.e: The NIA was constituted in 2009 under the provisions of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA.

questions.q: Who is the head of the State Executive Committee and also acts as the ex-officio CEO of the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)?
questions.e: The chairperson of the State Executive Committee (Chief Secretary) acts as the ex-officio chief executive officer of the SDMA.

questions.q: Which of the following are members of a Category I Cantonment Board? 1️⃣ Military officer commanding the station 2️⃣ Executive engineer 3️⃣ Health officer 4️⃣ Eight members elected by the people
questions.e: A Category I Cantonment Board includes the military officer commanding the station, an executive engineer, a health officer, and eight elected members, among others.

questions.q: Under the separate personnel system for municipalities, who controls the personnel?
questions.e: Under the separate personnel system, each local body appoints, administers, and controls its own personnel, and they are not transferable to other bodies.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council was established under which new Article of the Constitution?
questions.e: The 101st Amendment Act of 2016 inserted a new Article 279-A in the Constitution, which empowered the President to constitute a GST Council.

questions.q: What is the weighted vote share of all the State Governments combined in the GST Council?
questions.e: The votes of all the state governments combined have a weightage of two-thirds of the total votes cast in a meeting.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for the investigation of offences related to terrorism and has national ramifications?
questions.e: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) was set up as the central agency for the investigation of offences related to terrorism and other Acts with national ramifications.

questions.q: Who is the Chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA.

questions.q: Which of the following functions is performed by the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (SCs)?
o: To conduct elections for SC reserved seats
To appoint judges from the SC community
To inquire into specific complaints regarding deprivation of rights of SCs
questions.e: One of the core functions of the Commission is to inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the SCs.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson and how many other members?
questions.e: The Commission consists of a chairperson, a vice-chairperson, and three other members appointed by the President.

questions.q: To whom does the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) submit its annual report?
questions.e: The UPSC presents, annually, to the President a report on its performance.

questions.q: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was created in 1957 in pursuance of which Constitutional Article?
questions.e: In pursuance of Article 350-B, the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was created in 1957.

questions.q: Who is known as the "guardian of the public purse" in India?
o: The Chairman of the Finance Commission
questions.e: The CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and is the guardian of the public purse.

questions.q: Which law officer represents the Government of India in any reference made by the President to the Supreme Court under Article 143?
questions.e: The President has assigned the duty to the AG to represent the Government of India in any reference made under Article 143.

questions.q: NITI Aayog's Governing Council includes:
o: Chief Ministers of UTs with Legislatures
questions.e: The Governing Council comprises Chief Ministers of all States and UTs with Legislatures, and Lt. Governors of other UTs.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Chairperson and members of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (STs)?
questions.e: Under the Rules made by the President, the chairperson and members of the NCST hold office for a term of three years.

questions.q: Which body was described by Paul H. Appleby as a "Necessary but highly pedestrian function"?
questions.e: Paul H. Appleby criticized the CAG's function as a necessary but highly pedestrian one with a narrow perspective.

questions.q: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by:
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The advocate general of the state is appointed by the governor.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.e: The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body, not a constitutional one.

questions.q: What is the maximum age until which a member of the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) can hold office?
questions.e: The chairman and members of an SPSC hold office for six years or until they attain the age of 62 years.

questions.q: Under the 73rd Amendment, a person is NOT disqualified from the Panchayat if they have attained the age of:
questions.e: No person shall be disqualified on the ground that he/she is less than 25 years of age if he/she has attained the age of 21 years.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission falls under which administrative category?
questions.e: The Central Information Commission is a high-powered independent body established under the RTI Act, 2005; it is not a constitutional body.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the National Development Council (NDC)?
o: To appoint the Governor of a State
To audit the accounts of the Union
To prescribe guidelines for preparation of the national Plan
questions.e: One of the assigned functions of the NDC is to prescribe guidelines for the preparation of the national Plan.

questions.q: The Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) can hold office until the age of:
questions.e: The upper age limit for the Chairperson of the NCPCR is 65 years.

questions.q: Which officer compiles and maintains the accounts of state governments?
questions.e: The CAG compiles and maintains the accounts of state governments.

questions.q: The Attorney General of India is NOT debarred from:
o: Accepting directorship in companies without permission
Defending accused in criminal cases without permission
Advising against the Government of India
questions.e: The AG is not a full-time counsel for the Government and is not debarred from private legal practice.

questions.q: Who has the power to secure compliance of its decisions from a public authority under the RTI Act?
questions.e: The Information Commission has the power to secure compliance of its decisions from the public authority.

questions.q: The "Team India Hub" of NITI Aayog is responsible for:
questions.e: The Team India Hub carries out the mandate of fostering cooperative federalism and engagement with States.

questions.q: The National Commission for Minorities notifies 'minorities' based on which criteria according to the 1992 Act?
questions.e: The Central Government notifies 'minorities' for the purposes of the Act, and has notified six religious communities to date.

questions.q: Which of the following can be the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)? 1️⃣ Retired Chief Justice of India 2️⃣ Retired Judge of the Supreme Court 3️⃣ Serving High Court Judge
questions.e: The chairperson of the NHRC should be a retired chief justice of India or a judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Who appoints the Nyayadhikari of a Gram Nyayalaya?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The presiding officer (Nyayadhikari) shall be appointed by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.

questions.q: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has concurrent jurisdiction to investigate offences affecting:
questions.e: The NIA has concurrent jurisdiction to investigate and prosecute offences affecting the sovereignty, security, and integrity of India.

questions.q: The 74th Amendment Act makes it obligatory to set up a Family Court in cities with a population exceeding:
questions.e: It makes it obligatory on the State Governments to set up a Family Court in every city or town with a population exceeding one million.

questions.q: The first state to establish the institution of Lokayukta was:
questions.e: The institution of lokayukta was established first in Maharashtra in 1971.

questions.q: Which body serves as the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government of India?
questions.e: The NITI Aayog is the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government of India.

questions.q: Under PESA, which body must give a certification of utilization of funds for village projects?
questions.e: Every Panchayat at the village level shall be required to obtain from the Gram Sabha a certification of utilisation of funds for plans and projects.

questions.q: The Chairperson of the Finance Commission should be a person having experience in:
questions.e: The chairman of the Finance Commission should be a person having experience in public affairs.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council?
questions.e: The GST Council consists of the Union Finance Minister as the Chairperson.

questions.q: In the GST Council, what weightage is given to the votes of the Central Government?
questions.e: The vote of the central government shall have a weightage of one-third of the total votes cast in that meeting.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the CAG to inspect any office or department subject to his/her audit?
questions.e: Under the duties and powers (Article 149), the CAG has the power to inspect any office or department subject to audit.

questions.q: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as:
questions.e: The CEC can be removed from office on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The term of office for the Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes is:
questions.e: Under the Rules made by the President, the chairperson and members of the NCBC hold office for a term of three years.

questions.q: Who is the highest law officer in the State?
questions.e: The advocate general is the highest law officer in the state.

questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every:
questions.e: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year or at such earlier time as he/she considers necessary.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
questions.e: The Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 inserted Article 350-B regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

questions.q: The UPSC is the ______ recruiting agency in India.
questions.e: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is the central recruiting agency in India.

questions.q: The term of office of the Advocate General of a State is:
questions.e: The term of office of the advocate general is not fixed by the Constitution.

questions.q: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) is headed by a:
questions.e: The NIA is headed by a Director-General appointed by the central government.

questions.q: Who appoints the regional commissioners to assist the Election Commission?
questions.e: The President may appoint regional commissioners after consultation with the election commission.

questions.q: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are:
questions.e: Recommendations made by the Finance Commission are only of advisory nature and not binding on the government.

questions.q: Under PESA, what is the minimum reservation for Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats in Scheduled Areas?
questions.e: Reservation for the Scheduled Tribes shall not be less than one-half of the total number of seats in Scheduled Areas.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of members in the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), excluding the Chairperson?
questions.e: The NDMA consists of a chairperson (the Prime Minister) and other members, not exceeding nine in total.

questions.q: A person must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of which court to be the Attorney General of India?
o: High Court District Court Supreme Court
questions.e: The Attorney General must be a person who is qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Who is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department?
o: Finance Minister Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.e: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

questions.q: The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and how many other members?
questions.e: The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and four other members to be appointed by the President.

questions.q: The term of office for the Chairman and members of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is:
o: Five years or 65 years age Six years or 62 years age Six years or 65 years age
questions.e: The chairman and members of the UPSC hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years.

questions.q: Which official is the "guardian of the public purse"?
o: Finance Minister Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.e: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?
o: The President The Prime Minister  The Home Minister
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA.

questions.q: Which Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment Act?
questions.e: The 74th Amendment Act added a new Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution, containing eighteen functional items of municipalities.

questions.q: Who acts as the Chairman of the National Development Council?
questions.e: The Prime Minister of India is the chairman/head of the National Development Council.

questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted every ______ year.
questions.e: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year.

questions.q: Which organization is the "National Central Bureau" of Interpol in India?
questions.e: The CBI acts as the "National Central Bureau" of Interpol in India

questions.q: The term of office for the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is:
o: Three years  Five years Until age 70
questions.e: The Chairperson and members of the NCPCR hold office for a term of three years.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the GST Council?
o: Prime Minister Union Finance Minister  Union Revenue Secretary
questions.e: The GST Council consists of the Union Finance Minister as the Chairperson.
